title: Check the exact native binding and constructor before inferring API semantics from fields
applies_when: A cross-language constructor, wrapper, indexing operation, TMA descriptor or callback appears wrong from stored field names, a partial source excerpt, or another API with a similar signature; a Python-like GPU DSL slice is mistaken for a built-in list operation.
lesson: Inspect the exact version's constructor implementation and binding before inventing expected behavior. TVM C++ Range(begin, end) computes extent=end-begin; FromMinExtent is separate. T.Pipelined(start, stop) therefore does not become a min/extent API because its For consumer reads those fields. Check actual frontend IR with nonzero, equal and one-bound controls. Apply the same API-specific discipline to PyTorch advanced indexing versus index_copy_, signature binding/defaults, view bit counts and backend layout transformations. For CUDA cuTensorMapEncodeTiled, boxDim versus globalDim alone is not evidence of invalid encoding: consult rank, dtype, strides, interleave, swizzle and OOB rules, then use a native descriptor-only call with matching parameters and invalid controls before inventing a minimum-shape guard. Python-like syntax does not fix a DSL object's contract: pinned CUTLASS Array uses arr[start:count] for explicit vector slices. Thus acc[offset:4] accesses four elements even at a nonzero offset; replacing it with acc[offset:offset+4] changes the count. Trace the receiver's construction and exact __getitem__/__setitem__ implementation, not a Python-list surrogate. Prefer real native operations and matching registered tests over stand-ins that silently change the contract.
avoid_when: Constructor correctness does not prove later pipeline lowering or GPU execution. Descriptor acceptance does not prove a TMA load/store, OOB masking, synchronization or kernel numerics; one parameter set or GPU does not qualify other generated variants or target architectures. Python and C++ bindings, dependency revisions and neighboring operations may differ. A documented device guard does not qualify an alternative accelerator. A rank-zero shape still has one element times dtype bits and lanes, not zero storage. RoPE+SDPA may return BHSD from BSHD while plain SDPA preserves shape; a shape-preserving callback is not the same backend. Reopen with a supported caller and native failure at the actual failing stage; do not dismiss all constructor, indexing or layout bugs.

evidence.note: Explicit start/count vector loads assign count=idx.stop and offset the pointer by idx.start; vector stores do likewise at L2664-L2679. This is a pinned vendor source contract, not an installed dependency or GPU-kernel test. Open-ended, multidimensional, other-class and other-version slices need separate inspection.

acc_list contains cutlass.Array objects, not Python lists of registers; the kernel writes _acc_g[_o:4] at L932 and reads it at L970. The constructor plus vendor contract refutes the built-in-list rationale for changing these slices; it does not establish whole-kernel correctness or performance.

cuTensorMapEncodeTiled documents boxDim nonzero and <=256, innermost alignment, stride and swizzle restrictions, and OOB fill. It does not list a general boxDim[i]<=globalDim[i] requirement. This motivates a parameter-matched native API test; absence of that requirement alone is not measured encoding or kernel correctness.
Pinned vendored C++ Range constructor explicitly computes end-begin, except the equivalent zero-begin shortcut. Stored min/extent fields do not define the constructor's argument semantics.
Declares Range(begin,end) and a separate FromMinExtent; the min/extent constructor was removed to preserve the conventional range(begin,end) meaning.

Contributor checked pinned current-main source and four CPU-only native frontend controls on TileLang 0.1.15: nonzero/default and staged loops min=3,extent=2; one-bound 0,5; equal-bound 3,0. Not a current-main rebuild, lowering or GPU qualification.

Submitted repair of the already reported scalar view bug (#3378): current-main Python utility and registered CPU tests on release 0.1.15 TVM/TIRx bindings yield 7 baseline failures versus 16 patched passes. Includes scalar dtype/lane rejection and valid scalar/tensor rank changes. No GPU kernels, full source rebuild, performance or independent review acceptance is claimed.

The actual view consumer requires equal logical bit counts. Returning 1 before applying dtype bits and lanes for a rank-zero shape bypasses invalid-width rejection and rejects equal-bit-count scalar/tensor views; this is distinct from a zero-extent buffer.
RoPE+FP8 SDPA takes BSHD and returns BHSD; its fake implementation permutes accordingly. Plain SDPA differs. A shape-preserving callback misrepresents this backend.
Registered CPU fusion tests use a BHSD-returning RoPE callback matching the backend. Prefer that control; this source does not establish FA3 GPU qualification.
Device assertions precede Triton launch. CPU/meta rejection-wording tests do not validate another accelerator's cache writes, nor prove that backend unsupported.
The wrapper uses sig.bind and applies defaults before forwarding kwargs. Isolated lookup does not prove a positional/default bug; CUDA and skip_check/auto remain unqualified.

Advanced indexing permits CPU or same-device indices; a CPU boolean mask is not a CUDA device-error proof. index_copy_ instead requires index/source/destination on one device. These API-specific rules do not apply to all indexing operations.
